# An accumulator of one limb: add a product of the guarded factors

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `acc_mul_entry_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

A step of an accumulator: the running sum $t = \mathrm{RN}(s + x y)$, and the sum of the magnitudes $b$ rounded to a number of `T`:

$$t = \mathrm{RN}(s + x y), \qquad b = \mathrm{RN}(a + \lvert x\rvert \lvert y\rvert).$$

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `A.add_product(x, y)` | `Accumulator<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | `void` | one more term; the bound of the whole history is `A.error_bound()` ([Accumulator](accumulator.md)); not `constexpr`; each factor guarded (rule R3 on the factors of a fused operation) |
| `A.add_product(a, b)` | `Accumulator<T, 1>`, `T`, `T` | `void` |  |

`T` is `float` or `double`; `A` and `B` are accumulators, `kairn::Accumulator<T, k>`, header `kairn/accumulator.hpp`, which `kairn/kairn.hpp` includes. They take no marker: an operation of an accumulator compiles only while its kernels are proved ([The accumulator](accumulator.md)).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $a \ge 0$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $t = \mathrm{RN}(s + x y)$: the number of the format nearest to $s + x y$, ties to even.
- $b = \mathrm{RN}(a + \lvert x\rvert \lvert y\rvert)$: the number of the format nearest to $a + \lvert x\rvert \lvert y\rvert$, ties to even.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `acc_mul_entry_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/AccKernels.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/AccKernels.v), against `acc_mul_entry_1_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions acc_mul_entry_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition acc_mul_entry_1_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (1 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall s a x y : R,
  fmt emin prec s ->
  fmt emin prec a ->
  fmt emin prec x ->
  fmt emin prec y ->
  0 <= a ->
  let '(t, b) := acc_mul_entry_1 emin prec tie_even s a x y in
  fmt emin prec t /\
  fmt emin prec b /\
  t = RN emin prec (s + (x * y)) /\
  b = RN emin prec (a + ((Rabs x) * (Rabs y))).
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `acc_mul_entry_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** acc_mul_1 on the guarded x and y (rule R3, the factors of a fused operation). **License:** proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/acc_mul_entry_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/acc_mul_entry_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# acc.add_product(x, y) of Accumulator<T, 1> (milestone2.md, "The accumulator"): acc_mul_1 on x and
# y guarded (rule R3, the factors of a fused operation: architecture.md). acc_mul_1 only multiplies
# x and y, which R3 alone does not guard; but a compiler that sees one of them to be 1 rewrites
# fma(x, 1, s) as x + s and fuses a product x = a b of the program into that addition (Apple clang
# 21 under -ffp-contract=fast, measured). After the guards each is a number of the format. Its
# claims are those of acc_mul_1: the guard is the identity on numbers of the format.

gx = guard(x)
gy = guard(y)
t  = fma(gx, gy, s)
ax = abs(gx)
ay = abs(gy)
b  = fma(ax, ay, a)
```

## Measured

The stored brute-force runs of this kernel's code: the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound. A run is shown only if it ran the code the kernel has now: its generated C++ (scalar and packed, every kernel it calls inlined, with the functions it calls; comments left out) must be the same at the commit of the run, as the fingerprints in [`results/brute-code.json`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/results/brute-code.json) show ([How to read a page](reading.md#what-the-measured-numbers-are)).

**Milestone 2**: the runs of commit `5f597fb`, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#acc_mul_entry_1)).

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
